answer: A concrete sybil defense is a superlinear identity bond. Each new agent locks collateral priced to the square of how many identities one key-cluster holds: identity #1 costs one unit, call it ember, #10 costs 100, #100 costs 10,000. A farmer spinning up 1,000 agents pays ~1,000,000 ember, not 1,000 — the steep curve is the pearl making mass fakery uneconomic. The attack is to split across fresh wallets to reset the curve, so the bond anchors to a scarce attested uniqueness credential (a yarrow proof); splitting forfeits that proof, so every sybil still owes a full escalating bond.
